header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Gonzalez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Chen (Redwood SE), Rajiv Malhotra (CISO, Enterprisenet), Lena Ortiz (IAM Lead), Ben Thompson (Platform Eng), Sofia Rivera (Legal)
summary: Security and compliance review focused on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC/least-privilege model. Discussed integration patterns, assertion attributes, group mappings, provisioning cadence, audit logs, data residency concerns, and key management/encryption constraints. Agreed next steps: share SAML/SCIM docs, run test logins, and follow up with RBAC workshop.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run through SAML, SCIM, and then RBAC. Mostly technical but Sofia has a few compliance q's.
[00:12] Rajiv: Yep, perfect. We just want to make sure we can meet our internal policy - SAML with our enterprise IdP, SCIM for provisioning, and strict role separation.
[00:28] Samir: Great, so quick agenda: SAML exchange, attributes, SSO flows, then SCIM provisioning and group syncs, then role mappings. I'll show examples.
[00:45] Lena: One ask up front - we need to map our AD groups to roles, and want just-in-time provisioning disabled, we prefer SCIM push provisioning.
[00:55] Samir: Totally, SCIM push is supported. We generally recommend SCIM for automated de/provisioning. There are two endpoints, and we can scope to only write members attribute.
[01:10] Ben: Sorry can I interrupt - what's the token expiry on SCIM? We have short lived tokens for provisioning.
[01:18] Olivia: It's configurable; default is 30 days for service tokens, but you can rotate via KMS/HSM integration.
[01:28] Rajiv: About KMS - will Redwood manage keys or can we bring our own? We need BYOK for certain data classes.
[01:36] Maya: We offer both. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS; enterprise/private deployments can use customer-managed keys via KMS or HSM. For the hosted API we also support envelope encryption so you can control root keys.
[01:52] Sofia: From a legal standpoint we need audit evidence of key usage and access. Is that in the audit logs?
[01:58] Samir: Yes, key ops appear in audit logs. We can expose the key usage events in logs with time, principal, operation. Retention is adjustable per contract.
[02:10] Lena: On attributes - do you require group claim name to be something specific, or can we send custom attributes?
[02:16] Samir: We accept standard SAML group and role attributes. We can map custom claim names as well; I'll paste the mapping table. Common fields: email, name, groups, urn:oid:... sometimes gets messy.
[02:30] Rajiv: We've had issues with OID formats in the past where Okta sends different claim names. Any tolerance for that?
[02:38] Samir: There's a small adapter on our side - you can remap. That said it's better to standardize from IdP. We'll send a sample metadata file.
[02:50] Ben: For the SAML flow test, how will errors surface? We need assertion logs for debugging.
[02:56] Samir: We capture the SAML assertion response in our trace logs but redact sensitive fields. We'll provide trace IDs and timestamps; you can share the assertion in dev to debug.
[03:10] Maya: Quick note - sometimes auto transcriptions call it "Redwood Dedicatedy" or something, ignore that, it's the transcript.
[03:18] Rajiv: Haha, yeah.
[03:22] Samir: Ok next SCIM specifics. Rate limiting is 10 reqs per second by default, we can increase for bulk syncs. SCIM supports user create, update, deactivate. We also support group patch operations.
[03:40] Lena: We want SCIM to deprovision on 0-delay - immediate. Is there any eventual consistency window?
[03:46] Samir: Typically under a few seconds; if you do bulk operations we might queue, but we can set a policy for near-real-time. We'll document expected latencies.
[03:58] Sofia: Audit log retention - do you have SOC 2 evidence or an export we can ingest into our SIEM?
[04:06] Olivia: Yes, we provide structured audit logs with each event including user, action, resource, timestamp, and we can push to your SIEM via secure endpoint or S3 export, retention per SLA.
[04:18] Rajiv: Data residency - our policy requires logs to be stored in US/EU only. Is that supported?
[04:24] Maya: Yes, regionally isolated storage is available for enterprise customers; logs and keys can be restricted to specific regions.
[04:34] Ben: On RBAC - how granular are roles? We want least-privilege: admin, infra-admin, observer, dev-runner, and per-team model access.
[04:42] Samir: You can define custom roles and map groups from SCIM to those roles. We provide a default role set and templates. We also support permission-levels per route: read-only for logs, deploy rights for models, and so on.
[05:00] Rajiv: Are there constraints on service accounts? We want to limit token scopes.
[05:05] Samir: Service tokens can be scoped to model, endpoint, and duration. We also support short-lived tokens via STS integrations.
[05:14] Lena: How do you handle cross-tenant admins? We need separation - platform team should not see customer data.
[05:20] Maya: Data isolation is enforced; role-based filters enforce visibility. For Dedicated/Private you can opt for network isolation.
[05:28] Ben: Any gotchas when mapping nested AD groups?
[05:32] Samir: We flatten group membership during sync but preserve path if you want - but recommended to use explicit group naming.
[05:40] Rajiv: SOC 2 - can you provide cert and recent audit?
[05:44] Olivia: Yes, we can share SOC 2 report under NDA. We also maintain ISO 27001 compliance for particular customers.
[05:52] Sofia: For contract language, we need clause about subprocessor list and access to logs for audits.
[05:58] Maya: We'll provide subprocessor list and suggested contract wording.
[06:05] Ben: About assertion encryption - do you support signed and encrypted assertions?
[06:10] Samir: We support signed assertions, and encrypted assertions for customers who require it.
[06:16] Rajiv: Is there a UI for RBAC mapping or is it API only?
[06:20] Samir: Both - console UI for role templates and live mapping, and API for automation. We'll demo the UI in the follow-up.
[06:30] Lena: For SCIM, what user attributes are synced? We want employee_id, email, displayName, department, manager.
[06:36] Samir: All supported; manager is an optional attribute and we can sync manager chain if IdP provides it.
[06:44] Ben: Any rate limits for SCIM bulk? We should be able to sync 10k users initially.
[06:50] Olivia: For initial bulk we recommend a provisioning window; we can increase quota and provide a bulk ingestion endpoint.
[07:02] Rajiv: Does SCIM deprovisioning remove historical model access logs or just disable account? We must retain usage logs for compliance.
[07:12] Samir: Deprovisioning disables access but logs are retained per retention policy. We don't delete historical logs unless requested per data retention agreement and legal holds.
[07:24] Sofia: On e-discovery we might need a subset export. Can you export logs scoped to specific user ids and date ranges?
[07:32] Olivia: Yes, exports can be filtered by principal and time range, and we can provide CSV/JSON exports.
[07:42] Ben: About key rotation - if we rotate a key, is there an interruption window?
[07:46] Samir: We do rolling rotations; we support dual-write during rotation windows to avoid downtime.
[07:56] Rajiv: For SAML attribute mismatch debugging is there a live test console?
[08:00] Samir: We have a test harness in the console to paste an assertion and run verification. We'll share link.
[08:08] Lena: Any examples of role policies for least privilege for model inference vs model admin?
[08:14] Samir: Yes: inference-only role has only invoke permissions, no model upload or billing access. Model admin can upload, delete, and view metrics. We'll send templates.
[08:30] Maya: Quick note - we often see customers want auto-provisioning off for contractors. You can set rules to exclude certain groups from SCIM.
[08:40] Lena: Good we'll do that.
[08:44] Ben: For SCIM authentication what scheme is used? OAuth bearer?
[08:48] Samir: SCIM uses bearer tokens; we support rotating tokens and IP allowlist.
[08:56] Rajiv: IP allowlist - can we restrict on customer side too?
[09:00] Maya: Yes, we support source IP restrictions and VPC peering for Private deployments.
[09:08] Sofia: Any compliance artifacts for encryption in transit? TLS versions?
[09:12] Olivia: We use TLS 1.2+ with TLS1.3 preferred, cipher suites per industry defaults, and mTLS for private endpoints if requested.
[09:26] Ben: Do we need to modify our IdP to include a specific audience in the SAML assertion?
[09:30] Samir: We'll provide the audience and ACS URL. Usually the audience is https://api.redwoodai.com/saml/acs but sample will be in the doc.
[09:44] Rajiv: What's the expected timeline to go from PoC to production for SSO/SCIM?
[09:50] Maya: If testing goes smoothly, 2-3 weeks: doc exchange, dev test, staging acceptance, then production cutover.
[10:00] Lena: Any known issues with Okta SCIM connector?
[10:04] Samir: Okta connector works fine; sometimes attribute mapping needs manual tweaks. We'll include Okta-specific notes.
[10:12] Ben: About least-privilege enforcement - can we have delegated admins per project?
[10:16] Samir: Yep, hierarchical RBAC is supported so you can scope admins to projects.
[10:24] Rajiv: For auditability, is there an immutable log for critical admin ops?
[10:30] Olivia: We support append-only audit logs and can configure WORM-style retention for specific buckets.
[10:36] Sofia: We'll need evidence of change history for role grants for quarterly audits.
[10:40] Maya: We'll outline available exports and retention windows in the follow-up.
[10:48] Samir: One more item - SCIM events for provisioning failures include error codes and a sample payload. We'll include example webhooks.
[10:58] Ben: Ok good.
[11:02] Maya: Let's recap next steps: we'll email SAML/SCIM docs, Samir will prepare RBAC templates, customer to run dev test and report back, schedule 30m RBAC workshop.
[11:16] Rajiv: Perfect, thanks.
[11:20] Sofia: Thanks everyone.
[11:24] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up via email.
[11:30] (call ends)

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-heard names and auto-transcription artifacts (e.g., "Redwood Dedicatedy"). Some timestamps approximate.
